item.content:encoded:
BUTWAL: Three newly appointed ministers in Lumbini Province took the oath of office and secrecy on Tuesday.

Province Chief Krishna Bahadur Gharti Magar administered the oath to the newly appointed ministers from the Nepali Communist Party (NCP) at the Office of the Province Chief in Butwal.

Gharti Magar on Monday appointed Dipendra Kumar Pun as the Minister for Health, Indrajit Tharu as the Minister for Economic Affairs and Planning and Krishna Kushma Tharu as Minister for Agriculture, Land Management and Cooperatives on the recommendation of Chief Minister Chet Narayan Acharya.

CPN-UML formed a new alliance with the NCP in provinces after the Nepali Congress (NC) announced it was exiting the alliance with UML in late July.

Chief Minister Chet Narayan Acharya and Speaker Tularam Gharti Magar were also present at the swearing-in ceremony.

Province Chief Krishna Bahadur Gharti Magar on Monday appointed Dipendra Pun, Indrajit Tharu and Krishna Kushma Tharu of the CPN as ministers on the recommendation of Chief Minister Acharya as per Article 168(9) […]
item.content:encoded:
BUTWAL: Lumbini Chief Minister Chet Narayan Acharya has inducted three ministers from coalition partner the Nepali Communist Party (NCP) in his cabinet.

Province Chief Krishna Bahadur Gharti Magar on Monday appointed Dipendra Pun, Indrajit Tharu and Krishna Kushma Tharu of the CPN as ministers on the recommendation of Chief Minister Acharya as per Article 168(9) of the Constitution of Nepal, 2015.

The new ministers will be administered the oath of office and secrecy on Tuesday afternoon.

Dipendra Kumar Pun of Rolpa has been appointed as Minister for Health, Indrajit Tharu of Dang as the Minister for Economic Affairs and Planning, and Krishna Kushma Tharu of Bardiya as the Minister for Agriculture, Land Management and Cooperatives, according to the Office of the Province Chief.

Chief Minister Acharya has retained Tulsi Prasad Chaudhary as Minister for Forests, Environment and Tourism; Ramji Prasad Ghimire as Minister for Social Development; Santosh Kumar Pandey as Minister for Urban Development, Energy, Irrigation and Water Supply; Ratna Bahadur Khatri as Minister for Physical Infrastructure Development; and Bhandari Lal Ahir as Minister for Internal Affairs, Law, Industry and Transport.

Ahir represents Janata Samajbadi Party (JSP) Nepal, while the other four are from the CPN-UML.

item.content:encoded:
BUTWAL: The Lumbini Province Government has decided to provide relief to families affected by monsoon-related and other disasters.

The 15th meeting of the Provincial Disaster Management Council decided to provide immediate relief to families affected by disasters, which have caused significant loss of life and property, and to repair damaged roads and infrastructure.

The meeting, chaired by Chief Minister Chet Narayan Acharya, decided to release Rs 2.5 million from the Provincial Disaster Management Fund to reduce the risk of river erosion and flooding in the Susta area across the Narayani River in Susta Rural Municipality-5 of Nawalparasi.

The amount will be spent through the Water Resources and Irrigation Development Division Office, Nawalparasi.

Similarly, Rs 5 million will be released for the immediate repair and protection of the Uwa Khola bridge in Thabang Rural Municipality-5 of Rolpa. Floods have washed away one side of the bridge’s wing wall, while a large hole on the approach road has disrupted transportation, according to Bharat Mani Pandey, secretary at the Ministry of Home Affairs, Law, Industry and Transport.

Various sections of the Sulichaur-Thabang road have also been damaged and in need of immediate repair and safety measures. The amount will be spent through the Road Infrastructure Development Office, Rolpa.

The council also decided to send relief materials stocked at the warehouse of the Humanitarian Assistance and Provincial Emergency Operations Center to Rolpa. A consignment of 20 tents, 30 tarpaulins, 40 blankets, 48 mosquito nets, six kitchen sets and 20 mattresses has already been sent to Rolpa. It also decided to instruct the concerned ministry to use water supply pipes stocked at government offices to restore water supply projects damaged by wildfires, fires, floods and landslides.

As the risk of monsoon-related disasters remains, the council instructed the ministries and agencies leading the thematic disaster management “clusters” to hold immediate meetings and activate their respective clusters.

Chief Minister Acharya directed provincial agencies to ensure that disaster victims do not suffer further due to delays in rescue operations. Stating that heavy rainfall could still occur as the monsoon has not yet ended, he instructed all government agencies to remain on standby.

85 killed in monsoon-related disasters

Monsoon-related disasters in different parts of the province have claimed 85 lives so far.

According to the council, 91 monsoon-related disaster incidents have been recorded in the province so far. Thirteen people are injured while two are still missing.

Fifty-eight people died after drowning, four died in floods, three in lightning strikes and 20 in landslides.

Twenty people died in monsoon-related disasters in four local units of Rolpa, including 12 in Thabang alone. One is still missing.

Similarly, six people died in Sun Chhahari Rural Municipality, while one person each died in Lungri and Parivartan rural municipalities.

A total of 11 households have been displaced by disasters across the four local levels, while 318 households are at risk.

item.title: Lumbini Chief Minister Acharya passes floor test
item.dc:creator: bishnu

Forty-five lawmakers voted in favor of Acharya’s motion of confidence at a meeting of the Lumbini Provincial Assembly on Monday. A majority of 42 is needed to form a government in the 83-member provincial assembly. Acharya received backing from lawmakers of his […]
item.content:encoded:
BUTWAL: Lumbini Chief Minister Chet Narayan Acharya has secured a vote of confidence.

Forty-five lawmakers voted in favor of Acharya’s motion of confidence at a meeting of the Lumbini Provincial Assembly on Monday.

A majority of 42 is needed to form a government in the 83-member provincial assembly.

Acharya received backing from lawmakers of his party, the CPN-UML, the Nepali Communist Party (NCP) and the Janata Samajbadi Party (JSP) Nepal. Similarly, the Nepali Congress (NC) and Janamat Party voted against the motion, while the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) remained neutral.

Interestingly, JSP Nepal had withdrawn its support for Acharya’s government on Monday morning and instructed its lawmakers in the provincial assembly to vote against Chief Minister Acharya’s motion of confidence.

A total of 71 members participated in the vote. Twenty-six members voted against the motion, while eight lawmakers were absent on Monday.

Speaker Tula Ram Gharti Magar announced after the vote that Chief Minister Acharya had secured the confidence of the provincial assembly with 45 votes.

Acharya registered a motion of confidence after his coalition partner, the Nepali Congress, notified the provincial assembly secretariat of its decision to withdraw support for the government on July 28.

item.title: Disaster incidents claim 15 lives in Rolpa in two days
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: At least 15 people died in Rolpa over the past two days due to different disaster incidents. Inspector Krishna Shrestha, information officer at the District Police Office, Rolpa, told Himal Press over the phone that 10 people were killed in a landslide in Thabang on Wednesday night, while four others died in a landslide in […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: At least 15 people died in Rolpa over the past two days due to different disaster incidents.

Inspector Krishna Shrestha, information officer at the District Police Office, Rolpa, told Himal Press over the phone that 10 people were killed in a landslide in Thabang on Wednesday night, while four others died in a landslide in Sunchahari Rural Municipality on Thursday night. “Another person died after being struck by lightning in Khadar of Lungri Rural Municipality-1,” Shrestha added.

A landslide buried two houses in Phalbang of Sunchhahari Rural Municipality-2 on Thursday night. According to Shrestha, the deceased have been identified as Bir Bahadur Gharti Magar (77), Shani Gharti Magar (68), Lali Gharti Magar (70) and Lami Gharti Magar (64).

Earlier on Wednesday night, 10 people died when a landslide buried 11 structures in Kotalabara of Thabang Rural Municipality-5. Three are still missing.

Meanwhile, Nepali Communist Party (NCP) leader and member of the House of Representatives from Rolpa, Barsha Man Pun, met Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Friday and urged the government to step up efforts to rescue those still missing.

Pun also called for prompt medical treatment for the injured and compensation for the families of those killed in the disasters.

He urged the government to ensure long-term rehabilitation for families affected by the disasters.

The landslide struck Kotalbara in Thabang-5 on Wednesday night. “Although a joint search and rescue operation by the Nepali Army, APF Nepal, and the […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The death toll from a landslide in Thabang of Rolpa has risen to seven.

According to a statement issued by the Armed Police Force (APF) Nepal, five people are missing.

The landslide struck Kotalbara in Thabang-5 on Wednesday night.

“Although a joint search and rescue operation by the Nepali Army, APF Nepal, and the Nepal Police is underway, rescue workers are facing severe difficulties due to persistent rain and continuous mudslides,” the statement added.

Two injured, Himal Pun Magar (22) and Sanjaya Gharti Magar (25), have been sent to Butwal for further treatment.

The deceased have been identified as Shanti Pun Magar (18), Kamal Bahadur Pun Magar (65), Jun Kumari Pun Magar (40), Ashim Pun Magar (9), Ashok Pun Magar (6), Dal Bahadur Pun Magar (75) and Manarakhi Pun Magar (71).

“Three of the victims—one female and two males—were swept downstream and their bodies recovered along the banks of the Madi River in neighboring Pyuthan district, spanning Swargadwari Municipality and Mandavi Rural Municipality. Following the discovery, a disaster management team from the APF Pyuthan base was mobilized to assist in searching for the remaining missing persons.

Security forces are searching for the five missing residents: Ajambar Pun Magar, 80; Bal Bahadur Pun Magar, 78; Lil Bahadur Pun Magar, 72; Mani Pun Magar, 71; and Hastakala Pun Magar, 67.

The disaster completely buried several homes—including the residence of deceased victim Kamal Bahadur Pun Magar—and livestock sheds, causing significant loss of property and animals.

item.title: Three killed, 10 missing after landslide in Rolpa
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: ROLPA: Three people have died after a landslide buried seven houses and sheds, including the home of Kamal Bahadur Pun Magar, in Botlabara of Thabang Rural Municipality-5 in Rolpa district on Wednesday night According to DSP Panchakumar Bakhu, chief of the District Police Office, Rolpa, a 71-year-old woman was recovered dead from the landslide debris […]
item.content:encoded:
ROLPA: Three people have died after a landslide buried seven houses and sheds, including the home of Kamal Bahadur Pun Magar, in Botlabara of Thabang Rural Municipality-5 in Rolpa district on Wednesday night

According to DSP Panchakumar Bakhu, chief of the District Police Office, Rolpa, a 71-year-old woman was recovered dead from the landslide debris on Thursday morning.

Earlier, Shanti Pun Magar (18) and Kamal Bahadur Pun Magar, around 60, had been confirmed dead.

“Two injured, Himal Pun Magar (22) and Sanjay Gharti Magar (25), have been sent to a hospital for treatment,” DSP Bakhu said. “Ten are still missing.”

Police and local residents are searching for the people by clearing the debris.

The landslide occurred at around 8:45 pm when a slope above the settlement suddenly collapsed.

Police reached the incident site at 10:15 pm.

item.title: Lumbini Chief Minister Acharya to seek vote of confidence on Aug 17
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Lumbini Province Chief Minister Chet Narayan Acharya is set to seek a vote of confidence from the provincial assembly on August 17. Acharya, who is the parliamentary party leader of CPN-UML in the provincial assembly, is facing the floor test after the Nepali Congress (NC) withdrew its support for the provincial government on July […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Lumbini Province Chief Minister Chet Narayan Acharya is set to seek a vote of confidence from the provincial assembly on August 17.

Acharya, who is the parliamentary party leader of CPN-UML in the provincial assembly, is facing the floor test after the Nepali Congress (NC) withdrew its support for the provincial government on July 28.

As per Article 188 of the Constitution of Nepal, 2015, if a political party in the coalition provincial government withdraws its support, the chief minister must table a resolution in the provincial assembly for a vote of confidence within 30 days.

After NC announced its departure from the coalition with the UML, the UML has formed a new alliance with the Nepali Communist Party (NCP) to form governments in all seven provinces. As per the agreement between the two parties, UML will lead the government in Lumbini.

The two parties have reached an understanding to finalize portfolio allocations and expand the cabinet only after the Chief Minister Acharya passes the floor test. However, sources say the NCP has staked claims for three ministries, including the finance portfolio.

Lumbini Province has nine ministries, including the Office of the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers. Currently, the cabinet consists of the Chief Minister alongside four ministers from UML and two from Janata Samajbadi Party (JSP) Nepal.

Meanwhile, given the agreement reached at the central level with CPN (Masal), one ministry will also need to be allocated to the party.

Sources say initial discussions indicate that UML will get four ministries, including the Chief Minister, while NCP will get three, and JSP Nepal and CPN (Masal) will get one each.

A majority of 42 is needed to form a government in the 83-member provincial assembly. UML has 29 lawmakers, while NCP has 13, including the Speaker. Since the Speaker cannot vote, the coalition will need the support of additional parties to secure a majority.

UML-NCP alliance secures support of CPN (Masal) in Lumbini

item.dc:creator: bishnu

The two-point agreement was finalized following a discussion among UML Chairperson KP Sharma Oli, NCP Coordinator Pushpa Kamal Dahal and CPN (Masal) General Secretary Mohan Bikram Singh on Wednesday. The first […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The CPN-UML and the Nepali Communist Party (NCP) have reached a two-point agreement with CPN (Masal) to form a government in Lumbini Province.

The two-point agreement was finalized following a discussion among UML Chairperson KP Sharma Oli, NCP Coordinator Pushpa Kamal Dahal and CPN (Masal) General Secretary Mohan Bikram Singh on Wednesday.

The first point of the agreement states that the three parties will cooperate to form a government in Lumbini Province and carry out development work. Similarly, the second point states that the parties will collaborate on movements that support national sovereignty, the constitution, and the republic, while opposing regression.

CPN (Masal) has one member in the Lumbini Province Assembly.

A majority of 42 is needed to form a government in the 83-member provincial assembly. The UML and NCP, which have formed an alliance to form governments in all provinces, have a combined strength of 42.

UML has 29 members in the provincial assembly, while NCP has 13, including the Speaker. With Masal joining the alliance, the UML-NCP alliance has reached the magic number of 43.

item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Former mayor of Kapilvastu Municipality Kiran Singh has been found dead in a forest area.

According to the District Police Office, Kapilvastu, Singh’s body was found near his motorcycle on Sunday.

Superintendent of Police Manohar Bhatta, chief of Kapilvastu police, said members of the search team had found Singh’s motorcycle on Saturday.

The 65-year-old had left his home in Kapilvastu-3 at around 2 pm on Friday. CCTV footage showed the Nepali Congress (NC) leader heading toward Ramraj Bridge at around 3:27 pm, police say

After reaching the bridge, Singh reportedly contacted a person close to him by phone and said he had lost his way in the forest.

His relatives and local residents then began searching for him. On Saturday, they found his motorcycle parked in a forest area about eight kilometers from the East-West Highway.

Police, relatives and locals continued the search in the area. “The body was found near the location of his motorcycle, SP Bhatta said.

Police said further investigation into the incident is underway.
